# Versioning your own packages

This page is for developers who publish site packages and the packages they require, and need installations to pick
the right copy. It shows every place a version is written, how the kernel reads and compares them, and how to raise
them for a new release.

7x and the Exponential Foundation strongly encourage you to submit your packages by pull request to
se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth, where the release folders follow the Exponential versions: see
[Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md).

## Contents

1. [Where versions are written](#where-versions-are-written)
2. [How versions are compared](#how-versions-are-compared)
3. [What min-version does](#what-min-version-does)
4. [What the index version does](#what-the-index-version-does)
5. [Raising the version for a release](#raising-the-version-for-a-release)
6. [Published means permanent](#published-means-permanent)

## Where versions are written

| Place | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `package.xml` `<version><number>` | `1.2.0` | the package's version number |
| `package.xml` `<version><release>` | `1` | the release number of that version (1 for a new package) |
| `package.xml` `<changelog><entry release="...">` | `release="1"` | which release a changelog entry belongs to |
| `package.xml` `<require min-version="...">` | `1.2.0-1` | the lowest version of a required package this one accepts |
| `package.xml` `<ezpublish><version>` | `6.0.15-stable` | the Exponential version the package was made for (the element keeps its historical name) |
| `index.xml` `<package version="...">` | `1.2.0-1` | the version the server announces |
| the server folder | `exponential/6.0/6.0.15/` | the Exponential release the files were published for |

`eZPackage::getVersion()` joins number and release as `<number>-<release>`; that pair is what `min-version` and the
`ezpackage` table use. The `version` attribute of the root `<package>` element is something else: the kernel writes
the package format version there (`eZPackage::VERSION`, `3.5.2`) when it stores a package.

## How versions are compared

`kernel/classes/ezpackageversion.php` (`eZPackageVersion`) reads a version number as Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 first:

- `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, with optional `-prerelease` and `+build` (build metadata is ignored when comparing);
- older forms are still understood: fewer parts (`1.0` reads as `1.0.0`), more parts (`1.2.3.4`), a letter suffix
  (`3.4.0beta1` is the prerelease `beta1`);
- anything else is kept as text and sorts before every version that can be read.

The release number is compared last, numerically: `1.0-1` < `1.0-2` < `1.0.1-1`, and `1.0-1` equals `1.0.0-1`. In a
`<number>-<release>` pair, the part after the last `-` is the release only when it is all digits.

New packages from the creation wizards must have a strict SemVer version of at most 24 characters
(`eZPackageVersion::isValidNew()`); `ezpm create` takes the version as given. Use strict SemVer for your own packages:
it is the one form every tool reads the same way.

> **Note**
> The 7x site packages still carry `<number>6.0</number>` and `<release>15-stable</release>`, a form that predates
> these rules. Your fork does not have to copy it: reset the version to your own first release, for example
> `<number>1.0.0</number>` and `<release>1</release>`.

## What min-version does

When the setup wizard or the kickstarter installs a site package, `downloadDependantPackages()` in
`kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_site_types.php` looks at each `<require type="ezpackage">`:

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| the required package is not imported | it is downloaded from the `url` of its `index.xml` entry and imported |
| it is imported with a version lower than `min-version` (`eZPackageVersion::compareFull()`) | the old copy is removed and the package downloaded again |
| it is imported with that version or higher | it is used as it is |
| it is not in the index | the install stops with "Download of package '...' failed. You may upload the package manually." |

So raise `min-version` whenever your site package needs the newer content or classes; otherwise an installation that
imported an older copy keeps it.

## What the index version does

In the setup wizard in the browser, a site package that is both in the index and imported locally is offered from
the index when the index `version` is higher than the local one (`compareFull()` in `createSitePackagesList()`), and
the local copy is used otherwise. The kickstarter always prefers the index entry, because, as the code notes, "the
package index version attribute is not comparable with the local package version". Keep the index `version` equal to
`<number>-<release>` of the archive it points to, and both readings agree.

## Raising the version for a release

1. Raise `<number>` for a changed package (or `<release>` for a repackaging of the same content).
2. Add a `<changelog><entry release="...">` describing the change.
3. Raise `min-version` in every package that needs the change, and their versions in turn.
4. Rebuild the archives ([Rebuilding with build.sh](rebuilding-with-build-sh.md)).
5. Write the new versions into `index.xml`.
6. Publish into the folder of the Exponential release the packages are for
   ([Running your own package server](running-your-own-package-server.md)).

## Published means permanent

Once an archive is on a server, installations may have imported it under its version. Never replace a published
archive with different content under the same version: publish a new version, and say in its changelog what was wrong
with the previous one. A version whose last position reaches 9 goes on to 10 (`1.0.9` is followed by `1.0.10`);
only the last position counts on. The reasoning is on
[A pushed tag is permanent](../../designers/distribution/a-pushed-tag-is-permanent.md) and
[Only the last position counts](../../designers/distribution/only-the-last-position-counts.md).
